findings.title: Resolve the chain entry point from the installed wrapper
findings.body: OpenCode launches `pretool-dispatch.sh` with the project directory as its working directory. The proposed relative `hooks/pretool_chain.py` therefore resolves inside the project. An ordinary project will fail to load the chain, and a project containing that path will supply the code that decides whether its own operations proceed.

findings.title: Load the Antigravity module by its installed path under isolated Python
findings.body: The root `hooks.json` launches every bridge event with `python3 -I`. Isolated mode excludes the script directory from the import path, so an ordinary `import pretool_chain` fails in the packaged plugin. A top-level import failure also happens before the bridge can emit its fallback JSON, affecting SessionStart and Stop as well as PreToolUse.

findings.title: Preserve Antigravity’s fail-closed behavior when a skipped guard is broken
findings.body: The existing bridge test replaces the merge guard with a regular script that exits 3 and expects even `ls -la` to be denied. That file passes the proposed liveness checks, and `ls -la` has no landing keyword, so the dispatcher skips the failure and allows the call. The same gap applies to a regular script that times out or emits malformed JSON.

findings.title: Distinguish completed merge evaluation from silent guard failure
findings.body: A truncated merge guard can exit successfully with empty stdout. The imported `run_hook` accepts that as success, as it does `{}`, so a landing call can proceed without a verdict. The current branch has a completion marker and an explicit regression test for both cases. Moving the command into a skip-only corpus loses that coverage because a landing candidate runs the guard.

findings.title: Reconcile continuation-split commands with the unchanged guard’s input
findings.body: For the plan’s backslash-newline `push` example, normalization makes the prefilter run the guard. The unchanged guard then receives the original payload and splits it into lines without folding the continuation. It never sees the complete subcommand and can return empty. The promised end-to-end denial fails even though the prefilter property passes.

findings.title: Preserve blocking owner decisions when batching OpenCode patches
findings.body: On `origin/main`, OpenCode presents each patch target as `Edit` and blocks an owner-dispatch `ask`. For native `apply_patch`, `owner-dispatch.sh` explicitly converts that same `ask` into advisory `additionalContext`. In a non-strict opted-in repository, a patch touching gated code can therefore proceed where OpenCode previously stopped it. A test containing only a later **strict** denial misses this change.

findings.title: Retain OpenCode edit isolation when jq is unavailable
findings.body: With Git installed and jq missing, main’s OpenCode `blockReason()` still rejects edits in a `.worktree-only` primary checkout. The original shell isolation guard emits a warning and exits successfully in that environment. Making it the sole authority allows a protected edit, such as a text-file write, to proceed. The proposed dependency preflight covers Bash only.

findings.title: Keep checking the directory entry when a patch deletes or moves a symlink
findings.body: Restoring the original edit guard makes `host-input.py` resolve a leaf symlink before isolation is checked. If the link is in a protected primary checkout and its referent is outside, a patch can remove the protected entry. The R11 dispatcher checks both locations. Its existing end-to-end assertion would catch the regression, whereas a property tested only on skipped hooks would not.

findings.title: Give the whole chain a deadline below the host timeout
findings.body: The Claude registration and OpenCode adapter currently allow ten seconds for the entire dispatcher, while the bridge runner allows up to ten seconds per script. Two individually successful guards can exhaust the outer timeout before a decision is written. Claude can then proceed without the denial, or OpenCode can reject a merge after its grant has already been consumed. Both the Python and shell paths need time reserved to return the decision.

findings.title: Specify a blocking startup response when the shared core cannot run
findings.body: If Python exists but the installed module is missing or fails to load, a bare `exec` exits without producing a hook decision. On Claude, the plan itself notes that a crashed hook does not block. Consolidation makes that one startup failure disable every applicable guard. The missing-Python fallback and tests for failures *inside* `run_hook` do not exercise this case.

findings.title: Preserve hook-visible state when proving a skip safe
findings.body: In an opted-in repository, the Bash owner-dispatch hook can record a write for the Stop backstop and emit nothing. A prefilter that skips that call satisfies the proposed stdout property while removing the evidence Stop needs. Keep such hooks unconditional or test their state transitions and subsequent Stop outcome as part of the skip contract.

findings.title: Separate host-neutral verdicts from Antigravity’s output mapping
findings.body: The current `evaluate` represents both an explicit `allow` and no decision as `None`. It also chooses the permission reason over `systemMessage` and returns on a denial before collecting that hook’s context. Reusing it unchanged loses the explicit Claude release or its accompanying notice. Mapping `None` back to explicit `allow` instead would grant ordinary calls that should go through the host’s normal permission flow.

findings.title: Preserve Claude’s host identity when launching the merge guard
findings.body: The bridge’s `run_hook` deliberately removes `CLAUDECODE` from child environments. The merge guard requires `CLAUDECODE=1` along with a Claude transcript path to issue its explicit release. Reusing that environment on Claude consumes a valid one-shot grant but sends the user through another permission prompt, even if verdict composition is fixed.

findings.title: Preserve the original payload bytes for size-limited child hooks
findings.body: The bridge runner serializes the parsed payload again with default `json.dumps`. A valid UTF-8 Bash payload below 1 MiB can exceed that limit after non-ASCII text is escaped. `guard-broad-local-test.sh` reads only the first MiB, so it can receive incomplete JSON and silently allow an unscoped test run that the original payload would have blocked.

findings.title: Run the stateless broad-test guard before the one-shot skill checkpoint
findings.body: In this repository, an unscoped `pytest` command redirecting output into a shared skill file triggers both guards. `owner-dispatch-guard.sh` invokes `skill-loading.py`, which can spend the actor’s single implementation checkpoint before the broad-test guard runs. The command cannot execute anyway, and a later genuine edit loses its checkpoint. The R11 dispatcher checks test scope first.

findings.title: Preserve OpenCode’s subagent-start hook in the delegate chain
findings.body: OpenCode currently runs `subagent-start.sh` after a successful delegation check, enforces runner failure, and prepends the returned routing instructions to the worker prompt. The table includes that script only for Antigravity. Following it drops the context on OpenCode, while retaining the existing separate invocation breaks the stated single-call contract.

findings.title: Account for temporary-file failure before skipping the merge guard
findings.body: With working jq and Git but an unusable `TMPDIR`, the original merge guard emits a visible `mktemp failed` warning even for `echo ok`. The proposed preflight passes and the vocabulary filter skips the script, suppressing the warning. A property corpus run only with a healthy temporary directory will report success.

findings.title: Cover `pull` in the merge prefilter’s required vocabulary
findings.body: On the default branch, the original guard denies `git pull origin feature` because it merges another branch into the default branch. None of the listed trigger words occurs in that command. The list is explicitly incomplete, so I could not confirm whether the implementation would include `pull`. Pin this case with an asserted denial in a repository whose default branch is known.

findings.title: Match the broad-test guard’s escape handling before skipping it
findings.body: I checked the existing guard with the literal command `py\Xtest`. Its mask removes the backslash **and the following character**, producing `pytest` and a denial. The plan’s normalizer removes only the backslash, producing `pyxtest` and missing the runner. A trigger-word filter would change the verdict on this input.

findings.title: Preserve the documented dependency-degradation behavior
findings.body: If jq is missing, the proposed preflight denies every Bash call, including a command to diagnose or install jq. On main the merge guard emits a warning and exits successfully, and Antigravity accepts that result. This is a broader compatibility change than blocking a crashed script and contradicts the claim that Antigravity behavior stays unchanged.

findings.title: Define the shell fallback when jq is also unavailable
findings.body: On a host without Python or jq, the proposed fallback cannot use jq to select a chain or compose the result. Individual hooks can still emit literal degradation JSON, but the wrapper has no specified way to deliver a valid decision. The listed Python unit tests do not exercise the installed wrapper with both dependencies absent.

findings.title: Terminate hook descendants when a timeout expires
findings.body: The bridge uses `subprocess.run(..., timeout=...)`, which kills the direct shell process. A child started by that shell can survive and continue work after the dispatcher has returned. The current dispatcher has a process-group regression probe for exactly this case. Testing only that a timeout returns the right verdict would miss the leaked process.

findings.title: Validate the expanded binding inventory independently
findings.body: Removing a script from the shared `CHAIN` also removes it from `--bindings`. A comparison deriving its expected scripts from that same chain can stay green while all three hosts lose the hook. Separately, the packaged `antigravity.test.mjs` still expects literal equality with manifest command names, so changing only the named Python test leaves `make npm-publish-dry` failing on the wrapper entry.

findings.title: Preserve the scope of the human override
findings.body: The unchanged edit and merge denial messages tell users they can disable the individual guard through `/hooks`. With one registration, disabling it for a single edit exception also disables merge authorization, owner dispatch, and delegation checks. The plan needs a scoped release path if those existing overrides are to remain available.

findings.title: Keep sequence and host assertions when retiring dispatcher tests
findings.body: A corpus item cannot establish that a denied compound command leaves an armed grant intact, that the next authorized call consumes it exactly once, or that `ask`, `systemMessage`, and `additionalContext` reach the caller. For inputs where `may_act` is true, the proposed property makes no assertion at all. Deleting those behavioral tests would let ordering and output regressions pass.

findings.title: Adapt the benchmark before using it as an acceptance gate
findings.body: The R11 harness requires the complete OpenCode trace to contain only `pretool-dispatch.sh`, imports the Python dispatcher slated for deletion, and asserts the retired 2 MiB limit. A correct script-running replacement fails before the medians are reported. Its Claude baseline also runs registrations serially, overstating main’s wall-clock latency, and it measures no Antigravity call.

findings.title: Exercise the Codex consumer of the shared manifest
findings.body: Codex also consumes `hooks/hooks.json`. The listed host smoke checks plugin registration, while the real tool-call smoke is Claude-only. A composed response that emits an unsupported explicit `allow` on Codex, or mishandles its `apply_patch` input shape, can pass both checks. Preserve a Codex-shaped tool-call and response assertion in the replacement suite.

findings.title: Run the repository’s complete verification lane
findings.body: The proposed “full lanes” omit `test-code-review`, one of the three required `make test` dependencies. The current Makefile also invokes `hooks/test_pretool_dispatch.py`, which the plan removes. Without rewiring that target and running `make test`, the documented checks can either stop on a deleted file or leave a required regression family unverified.
